docs.title: khflutterlib
docs.text: khflutterlib is the shared Flutter foundation for product teams building company apps from a consistent set of core primitives, design tokens, reusable UI, and screen patterns. It is a monorepo of independently versioned packages that are consumed by applications through git-based dependencies rather than a single published package.

docs.title: What this monorepo includes
docs.text:
• kh_core for shared constants, result/failure types, config, and base domain patterns
  • kh_theme for design tokens and assembled Material theme data
  • kh_ui for reusable widgets such as buttons, fields, cards, dialogs, and states
  • kh_screens for composed screen-level patterns built on the lower-level packages
  • packages/example as a runnable component gallery for visual QA and integration checks

docs.text:

├── packages/
│   ├── kh_core/

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Flutter 3.44.1 stable
  • Dart >= 3.9.0 < 4.0.0
  • Melos 7+

Install Melos:

dart pub global activate melos

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
From the repo root:

cd flutter
melos bootstrap

This installs dependencies for every package in the workspace and prepares the monorepo for local development.

Run the example gallery:

cd packages/example
flutter run

Run checks across packages:

melos run analyze
melos run test
melos run test:flutter

docs.title: Package guidance
docs.text:
Use the package that matches the layer you need in your app:

  • kh_core for common primitives and domain contracts
  • kh_theme for theme and design-system setup
  • kh_ui for reusable widgets and shared form patterns
  • kh_screens for full-screen flows such as splash or onboarding screens

docs.title: Consumer app dependency pattern
docs.text:
Apps consume the monorepo via git dependencies, not pub.dev:

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  kh_core:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_core
      ref: kh_core-v0.1.1
  kh_theme:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_theme
      ref: kh_theme-v0.1.1
  kh_ui:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_ui
      ref: kh_ui-v0.1.1+1

This is the intended integration model for a separate application, and it matches the repo's current architecture and release flow.

docs.title: Typical app setup
docs.text:
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:kh_theme/kh_theme.dart';
import 'package:kh_ui/kh_ui.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MyApp());

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      theme: KhTheme.light(),
      darkTheme: KhTheme.dark(),
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: KhButton.primary(
            onPressed: () {},
            child: const Text('Continue'),
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}

docs.title: Notes and expectations
docs.text:
• kh_core stays intentionally free of Flutter dependencies where possible.
  • kh_theme is the visual baseline for every package in the library.
  • kh_ui wraps standard Material widgets and keeps the app-level customization model straightforward.
  • kh_screens is intended to provide higher-level product flows built on the reusable primitives below it.

This repo is most useful when consumed as a coordinated library family rather than as a single app, and these docs are organized to make that consumer pattern obvious.

docs.title: Core
docs.text: The kh_core package contains the shared domain and infrastructure primitives that the rest of the library is built on. It is intentionally designed to be as close to pure Dart as possible, so it can be used in tooling, tests, and platform code without requiring the Flutter SDK for every situation.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
kh_core is responsible for:

  • app environment definitions and bootstrap config
  • result/failure error modeling
  • base entities and repository contracts
  • validation and utility extensions
  • common retry, debounce, and pagination helpers

docs.title: Status
docs.text: This package is under active development and is a foundational dependency for the later packages in the monorepo.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dependencies:
  kh_core:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_core

docs.title: Main exports
docs.text: Symbol Purpose KhEnvironment enum for environment values such as development/staging/production KhEnvironmentConfig app-level environment configuration loaded once at bootstrap KhResult<T> typed success/failure return model KhFailure root failure type for typed errors KhException thrown exception model for infrastructure code KhEntity<I> base entity with identity semantics KhPage<T> paginated collection model KhReadRepository<T, ID> read-only repository contract KhMutableRepository<T, ID> write-capable repository contract KhDebouncer debounced repeated actions KhRetry retry wrapper for failure-prone operations

docs.title: Environment setup
docs.text:
Bootstrap once at app startup:

import 'package:kh_core/kh_core.dart';

void main() {
  KhEnvironmentConfig.initialize(
    KhEnvironmentConfig(
      environment: KhEnvironment.fromString(
        const String.fromEnvironment('ENV', defaultValue: 'development'),
      ),
      apiBaseUrl: const String.fromEnvironment('API_BASE_URL'),
      enableLogging: true,
    ),
  );

  runApp(const MyApp());
}

This pattern allows the application to read the same configuration from all layers without passing environment values around manually.

docs.title: Result and failure handling
docs.text:
The library uses KhResult<T> to model operations that may succeed or fail without relying on exceptions as the primary return type.

import 'package:kh_core/kh_core.dart';

KhResult<String> fetchName() {
  try {
    return const KhResult.success('Ada');
  } on Exception {
    return const KhResult.failure(
      KhValidationFailure('Unable to fetch user name'),
    );
  }
}

final result = fetchName();
final text = result.fold(
  onSuccess: (value) => value,
  onFailure: (failure) => failure.message,
);

This makes domain code and UI logic much easier to reason about when the same method can either return data or an explicit failure.

docs.title: Base entity model
docs.text:
Use KhEntity<I> for domain objects with a stable identifier:

class User extends KhEntity<String> {
  const User({required this.id, required this.name});

  @override
  final String id;

  final String name;
}

The identity is used for equality semantics rather than every field being compared.

docs.title: Pagination and repository contracts
docs.text:
KhPage<T> makes list handling consistent across the library:

final page = KhPage<User>(
  items: const [User(id: '1', name: 'Ada')],
  page: 1,
  pageSize: 20,
  totalCount: 1,
);

if (page.hasNextPage) {
  // continue fetching
}

Repository interfaces are deliberately small and composable:

abstract class UserRepository implements KhMutableRepository<User, String> {}

docs.title: Common utilities
docs.text:
kh_core also exposes a small set of everyday helpers for formatting, validation, retry, and timing.

final validEmail = 'ada@example.com';
final isEmail = KhRegex.email.hasMatch(validEmail);

final debouncer = KhDebouncer(const Duration(milliseconds: 300));
debouncer.run(() => print('debounced'));

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Call KhEnvironmentConfig.initialize() before reading KhEnvironmentConfig.current.
  • Use KhResult.guard or KhResult.guardAsync for conversion between thrown exceptions and typed failures.
  • Prefer explicit domain failures over generic errors when the cause matters to the caller.

docs.title: Screens
docs.text: The kh_screens package adds composed, app-level screen patterns that are built on top of kh_ui and kh_theme. It is intended for flows such as launch screens, onboarding, and authentication entry points that are shared across apps.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text: kh_screens provides reusable high-level screens and patterns, instead of forcing every consumer app to rewrite common entry flows.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: This package is under active development and is meant to complement the lower-level widget and theme packages.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dependencies:
  kh_screens:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_screens

docs.title: Example: splash screen
docs.text:
import 'package:kh_screens/kh_screens.dart';

KhSplashScreen(
  logo: Image.asset('assets/logo.png', width: 140),
  initialize: () => sessionRepository.restore(),
  onInitializationComplete: () {
    Navigator.of(context).pushReplacementNamed('/home');
  },
);

This pattern lets the app keep the splash state and initialization logic independent from routing decisions.

docs.title: Design goals
docs.text:
• keep product flows reusable
  • avoid repeated app-level implementations of common app entry screens
  • stay flexible enough for app-specific customization
  • rely on the lower-level packages for base styling and behavior

docs.title: Considerations
docs.text:
• initialize should fail gracefully and be wrapped in app-level error handling.
  • Splash or onboarding screens should not lock the app to a specific router implementation.
  • The screen should defer to the theme rather than hard-code colors or spacing values.

docs.title: Theme
docs.text: The kh_theme package defines the design system for the monorepo. It is the primary package for color tokens, typography, spacing, borders, and assembled ThemeData objects used across the other packages.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
kh_theme provides:

  • a default seed-based brand palette
  • semantic colors for success, warning, and info states
  • a Material type scale and spacing model
  • a theme extension for app-specific semantic values
  • ready-to-use KhTheme.light() and KhTheme.dark() builders

docs.title: Status
docs.text: This package is available and is the standard styling layer for kh_ui and kh_screens.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dependencies:
  kh_theme:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_theme

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:kh_theme/kh_theme.dart';

MaterialApp(
  theme: KhTheme.light(),
  darkTheme: KhTheme.dark(),
  home: const Scaffold(
    body: Center(
      child: Text('Hello from kh_theme'),
    ),
  ),
);

You can also supply a custom seed color:

MaterialApp(
  theme: KhTheme.light(seedColor: Colors.teal),
  darkTheme: KhTheme.dark(seedColor: Colors.teal),
);

docs.title: Token categories
docs.text:
kh_theme intentionally separates the structural tokens from the brand seed:

final spacing = KhSpacing.md;
final radius = KhRadius.md;
final elevation = KhElevation.level2;
final accent = KhColors.brandSeed;

The app can adjust the seed color while keeping the rest of the design system stable and coherent.

docs.title: Semantic colors
docs.text:
The theme extension exposes semantic values that Material's default color scheme does not cover well:

final theme = Theme.of(context).extension<KhThemeExtension>();
final successColor = theme?.success ?? Colors.green;

This is useful when you need consistent appearance for validation, success, info, and warning states in app interfaces.

docs.title: Typography
docs.text:
KhTypography defines the design-system type scale, which is applied through the assembled ThemeData:

final title = KhTypography.headlineMedium;
final label = KhTypography.labelLarge;

The default font is the local Inter asset included with the package, unless the consuming app overrides it at theme creation time.

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Prefer theme-driven styling over hard-coded colors in widget code.
  • Use Theme.of(context) and KhThemeExtension to read semantic values.
  • Keep customizations at the app boundary, not inside every individual widget.

docs.title: UI
docs.text: The kh_ui package provides the reusable UI toolkit for the monorepo. It wraps common Material widgets and keeps the app-level customization model consistent with the design system created by kh_theme.

docs.title: Package purpose
docs.text:
kh_ui includes high-value widgets for common product interfaces:

  • KhButton for consistent buttons and icon buttons
  • KhTextField for themed form inputs
  • KhCard for content containers
  • KhDialog for alerts and confirmations
  • KhLoadingState, KhEmptyState, and KhErrorState for screen states
  • KhChip and KhBadge for status-style indicators

docs.title: Status
docs.text: The package is active and used as the building block layer for product UI.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dependencies:
  kh_ui:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/msflib/flutter.git
      path: packages/kh_ui

docs.title: Button usage
docs.text:
import 'package:kh_ui/kh_ui.dart';

KhButton.primary(
  onPressed: () {},
  child: const Text('Continue'),
);

KhButton.outline(
  onPressed: () {},
  child: const Text('Cancel'),
);

These constructors follow the app's configured theme rather than hard-coded colors or dimensions.

docs.title: Text field usage
docs.text:
KhTextField(
  decoration: const InputDecoration(labelText: 'Email'),
  keyboardType: TextInputType.emailAddress,
  validator: (value) => value == null || value.isEmpty ? 'Required' : null,
);

kh_ui values theme defaults while still allowing a single input to override a specific decoration detail.

docs.title: Card and dialog usage
docs.text:
KhCard(
  child: Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.all(16),
    child: Text('Card content'),
  ),
);

KhDialog.alert(
  context: context,
  title: 'Ready',
  content: 'Your changes are saved.',
);

docs.title: Screen-state components
docs.text:
KhErrorState(
  failure: KhValidationFailure('Something went wrong'),
  onRetry: () {},
);

These states are intended to keep user feedback consistent across screens without requiring each screen to reinvent the same UI patterns.

docs.title: Theming principle
docs.text: Every widget in kh_ui should prefer Theme.of(context) over direct token reads. This keeps the package flexible for consuming apps that customize the brand color or font family using KhTheme.
